title: Beyond Consensus: Perspectivist Modeling and Evaluation of Annotator Disagreement in NLP

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying multi-annotator modeling architectures (latent-truth, task-based, and embedding-based methods) that capture individual and group-level variations, modeling disagreement as a meaningful signal rather than noise.

Reviewing diagnostic fairness evaluation frameworks (such as AART and PERSEVAL) that measure group-level disparities, disaggregated performance metrics, and parity gaps across annotator demographic identities.
Reviewing prior literature that demonstrates how an annotator's political orientation systematically correlates with subjective judgments in tasks like toxicity detection.
Reviewing studies showing disparities in how models and annotators treat specific dialects, such as the correlation between racial attitudes and judgments of African American English.
